findings.reason: a worker reasoning from "the join is the serialiser" can keep a synchronous path for `lifetime_deadline is None` — the common fresh-arming branch and the one measured — believing something else already serialises it, which preserves exactly the stall the section exists to remove.
findings.text: the deliverable says "Today that join is what keeps sweeps sequential", but `_sweep_on_cadence` has two branches (`reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1877-1891`): with no lifetime deadline it calls `_sweep_quietly()` **inline**, and only with one does it start a thread and `poll.join(remaining)`. The measured follower (session `a337e0e6`, armed 2026-11-07T12:13:44Z, still leased at 04:48Z on 9 November) ran far past any arming grant, and `_carried_lifetime_deadline` (`:281`) carries an original deadline across reloads without extending it, so its `lifetime_deadline` was `None` and its sweep ran on the inline branch — there was no join in play, and the inline call is what serialised its sweeps. Naming the join as the serialiser misdescribes the branch the section's evidence comes from and leaves the inline branch's loss of serialisation unaccounted for.
